```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
unlink("ingest-predictors.evolanddb", recursive = TRUE)
set.seed(143)
library(evoland.plus)
library(data.table)

# a database whose coordinates lie on the grid of a synthetic landscape
landscape <- synthetic_landscape(n_periods = 1, n_cells = 40)
db <- evoland_db$new(path = "ingest-predictors.evolanddb")
db$coords_t <- create_coords_t_square(
  epsg = 3857L,
  extent = terra::ext(landscape$drivers),
  resolution = 100
)

# one driver of the landscape, written out as the GeoTIFF we pretend to download
source_dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "predictor-sources")
dir.create(source_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)
geotiff <- file.path(source_dir, "accessibility.tif")
terra::writeRaster(landscape$drivers[["accessibility"]], geotiff, overwrite = TRUE)
```

*Note: this how-to guide assumes that you know the basic `evoland.plus` workflow from the [tutorial](evoland.plus.html).*

Predictors usually come as files, such as GeoTIFFs from a data provider.
This guide reads one GeoTIFF onto the coordinate points of an `evoland_db` and records where it came from.
So that the guide runs without network access, a hidden setup chunk has written a synthetic GeoTIFF, `accessibility.tif`, to a temporary directory, on the same 100 m grid as the coordinate points of `db`.

# Download and verify the file

`download_and_verify()` takes a table of URLs and their MD5 checksums, downloads each file into a cache directory, and warns if a file does not match its checksum.
Our file is local, so its URL uses the `file://` scheme; the commented lines show how remote files are listed.

```{r}
#| label: download
sources <- data.table(
  url = paste0("file://", geotiff),
  # url = "https://example.org/archive/accessibility.tif",
  # url = "ftp://ftp.example.org/drivers/accessibility.tif",
  md5sum = unname(tools::md5sum(geotiff))
)

fetched <- download_and_verify(
  sources,
  target_dir = file.path(tempdir(), "evoland-cache")
)
fetched[, .(local_filename, checksum_matches = md5sum == md5sum_actual)]
```

The checksum matches, and `fetched$local_path` holds the path of the cached copy.
Files already in the cache are not downloaded again.

# Read the raster and extract its values

We read the cached file with `terra` and extract one value per coordinate point with `extract_using_coords_t()`.

```{r}
#| label: extract
accessibility_at_coords <-
  terra::rast(fetched$local_path) |>
  extract_using_coords_t(db$coords_t)
accessibility_at_coords
```

Each of the 1600 coordinate points received a value.
`extract_using_coords_t()` reads the raster cell that contains each point, without resampling; a raster on another grid should first be brought onto the grid of the coordinates, e.g. with `terra::project()` or `terra::resample()`.
It also accepts a `SpatVector`, see `?extract_using_coords_t`.

# Add the predictor

`$add_predictor()` stores the values together with their metadata.
Accessibility does not change over time, so we store it under the static period `0`.
The `sources` table goes into the predictor metadata, so that the file can be fetched and verified again later.

```{r}
#| label: add-predictor
db$add_predictor(
  pred_data_raw = accessibility_at_coords[, .(id_coord, id_period = 0L, value)],
  name = "accessibility",
  fill_value = NA,
  pretty_name = "Accessibility",
  description = "Driver of the synthetic landscape, see ?synthetic_landscape",
  orig_format = "GeoTIFF, EPSG:3857, 100 m",
  sources = sources
)
db$pred_sources_v
```

`db$pred_sources_v` lists the URL and checksum of every predictor's sources: the table to pass to `download_and_verify()` to rebuild the cache on another machine.
